title: Support multiple items of the same type in DataTransfer API for drag and drop

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
Drag and drop APIs on operating systems like macOS and iOS and possibly others are implemented in terms of drag items. A drag can contain one or more items, and these items can be of the same type. For example, you can select multiple emails on macOS and drag them, or multiple files in Finder. The current DataTransfer API used for drag events only supports a single item of a given type (except for files, where multiple are supported). This includes both the older `getData`/`setData` APIs, and, inexplicably (IMO), the newer `DataTransferItemList#add` API, which throws if you add a second item of the same type.

It would be very useful for web applications to be able to drag and drop multiple items at once for more types than just files. Currently, the only way to do this is to resort to hacks like concatenating the items together into a single item using a serialization format like JSON. This works, but only within the same application. If you wanted to support interoperability with other applications (either native or web) using a more standard format, it is not possible. This is also true of receiving drops from native apps, which can drag multiple items but only the first one will be received by the web app.

This already results in broken behavior on some devices like the iPad, which supports adding items to an existing drag session once it has been started. You can start dragging a single item, and use the data transfer API to set data for that one item, but then the user can tap on another item to add it to the drag session. This again calls `dragstart` and sets the data, and it is added to the existing drag. Dropping in a native app shows both items, but dropping in a web app only allows access to the first one (if they are the same type). This results in a broken experience where the user expects multiple items to be dropped but only gets a single one.

My proposal would be for the `DataTransferItemList#add` API to support multiple items of the same type, while `setData` would continue to replace all items of that type with the new value. IMO this makes sense from an API point of view as `add` implies adding an item, not replacing.

I'm filing a spec issue because it is explicitly [not allowed by the spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dnd.html#datatransferitemlist) to support multiple items of the same type, and therefore browsers are currently implementing it "correctly". If it makes more sense to file browser issues first and then backport it to the spec, that's fine too, but I figured I'd start here and get feedback.
